description.narrative: Contract related to: Establishing a Victims¿ Registry in Sudan: Laying the Foundation for Future Reparation - After over three years of war, the conflict in Sudan continues to have devastating consequences, facing the world¿s largest humanitarian and displacement crisis with over 14 million displaced people. The EU adopted the Council conclusions on Sudan on 20 October 2025, spelling out four key asks to all parties to the conflict: ceasefire, humanitarian access and protection of civilians, civilian governance and accountability. Against this background, this exceptional assistance measure will scale up support to local responders in the provision and rehabilitation of essential services, complemented with interventions to reduce explosive ordnance contamination, thereby enabling aid assistance and returns. It will also enhance the inclusion aspects of the political and mediation processes, including by accompanying civilian actors to participate in such processes, within and beyond the Quintet¿s efforts. Finally, the measure will contribute to transitional justice foundations, in particular to support victims of conflict-related sexual violence.
